emerging_themes.evidence: Counts increased consistently from 707 (2026-08-10) to 753 (2026-08-17) and rose significantly to 1099 by 2026-09-14 at a fixed dataset size of 23,169 records.
emerging_themes.risk_statement: Customers may be experiencing increased hesitancy or requiring higher validation before trying new products or completing initial purchases.
emerging_themes.recommended_monitor: Track conversion rate on product detail pages for non-repeat items and monitor customer queries regarding product authenticity, freshness guarantees, or delivery timelines.

emerging_themes.evidence: Counts nearly doubled from 321 (2026-08-17) to 604 (2026-09-14) while total volume analyzed remained constant at 23,169 records.
emerging_themes.risk_statement: Dark store stockouts or poor substitution recommendations may be causing friction, potentially eroding customer trust during checkout.
emerging_themes.recommended_monitor: Monitor out-of-stock rates, fill rates across key dark stores, and user acceptance rates of suggested item substitutions.

emerging_themes.evidence: Counts dropped from 341 (2026-08-17) to 237 (2026-09-14) within identical sample sizes.
emerging_themes.risk_statement: Repeat customers may be reducing order frequency or encountering friction in reordering daily essentials.
emerging_themes.recommended_monitor: Track week-over-week repeat order rates, usage of 'Buy Again' navigation entry points, and retention cohorts for core categories.

new_problem_hypotheses: Increased availability and substitution issues directly correlate with a drop in habit/repeat purchases as users fail to find their regular SKUs.
Rising trial confidence issues suggest recent platform changes or product assortment shifts are causing first-time buyers to seek additional reassurance before placing orders.
analysis.caveat: Data points prior to 2026-08-10 reflect rapidly changing underlying record counts during pipeline backfills or test periods; trends are derived primarily from the stable snapshots between 2026-08-10 and 2026-09-14.
